١٠٥٥٠ — عن عتبة بن عبد أن رجلًا قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، العن أهل اليمن، فإنهم شديد بأسهم، كثير عددهم، حصينة حصونهم. فقال: ((لا)). ثم لعن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ الأعجمين: فارس والروم، وقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إذا مر بكم أهل اليمن يسوقون نساءهم، ويحملون أبناءهم على عواتقهم، فإنهم مني وأنا منهم)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧٦٤٧)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٧/١٢٣).

10550 — ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd narrated that a man said:
“O Messenger of Allah, curse the people of Yemen, for they are mighty in warfare, numerous in number, and their fortresses are strong.”
He replied:
“No.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then cursed the non-Arab powers of Persia and Rome.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said:
“When the people of Yemen pass by you, driving their women and carrying their children upon their shoulders, then they are from me and I am from them.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (17647) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (17/123).

١٠٥٥١ — عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت: ﴿إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللّٰهِ وَالْفَتْحُ﴾ حتى ختم السورة، قال: نُعيت لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ نفسه حين نزلت. قال: فأخذ بأشد ما كان قط اجتهادًا في أمر الآخرة. وقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بعد ذلك: ((جاء الفتح، ونصر اللّٰه، وجاء أهل اليمن)). فقال رجل: يا رسول اللّٰه، وما أهل اليمن؟ قال: ((قوم رقيقة قلوبهم، لينة قلوبهم، الإيمان يمانٍ، والفقه يمانٍ)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (١١/٣٢٨-٣٢٩). ورواه من طريق آخر (١١٩٠٤)، وزاد فيه: ((والحكمة يمانية)).

10551 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
When the verse,
“When the victory of Allah and the conquest come…”
was revealed through to the end of the sūrah, it announced to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that his death was approaching.
He then exerted himself in matters of the Hereafter more intensely than ever before.
After that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The conquest has come, the victory of Allah has come, and the people of Yemen have come.”
A man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, who are the people of Yemen?”
He replied:
“They are a people whose hearts are tender and gentle. Faith is Yemeni, and understanding of the religion is Yemeni.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (11/328–329).
He also narrated it through another chain (11904), which adds:
“And wisdom is Yemeni.”

حسن: رواه أحمد (١٤٦٩٠).

10552 — Jābir said:
One day, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he looked toward al-Shām and said:
“O Allah, turn their hearts toward You.”
He then looked toward Iraq and said something similar. He looked toward each direction and did the same.
He also said:
“O Allah, provide us with the fruits of the earth and bless us in our mudd and our ṣāʿ.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (14690).

“O Allah, turn their hearts toward obedience to You and protect them from behind.”

The words “protect them from behind” mean: preserve and guard them. The expression comes from the Arabic verb ḥāṭa–yaḥūṭu, meaning to protect and safeguard.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked toward Yemen and said:
“O Allah, turn their hearts toward You.”
He looked toward Iraq and said:

He then looked toward al-Shām and said:
“O Allah, turn their hearts toward You and bless us in our ṣāʿ and our mudd.”

١٠٥٥٥ — عن أبي برزة قال: بعث رسول اللّٰه ﷺ رجلًا إلى حي من أحياء العرب، فسبوه وضربوه، فجاء إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فأخبره، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لو أن أهل عُمَان أتيت، ما سبوك ولا ضربوك)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٤٤/٢٢٨).
وقوله: «عُمَان» بضم العين وتخفيف الميم، وهو الإقليم المعروف في جزيرة العرب. وحكى القاضي أن منهم من ضبطه بفتح العين وتشديد الميم، يعني عَمَّان البلقاء، وهذا غلط.

10555 — Abū Barzah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man to one of the Arab tribes. They insulted and beat him.
The man returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of what had happened.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Had you gone to the people of Oman, they would neither have insulted you nor beaten you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2544/228).
The name ʿUmān is pronounced with a ḍammah on the letter ʿayn and an ungeminated mīm. It refers to the well-known region in the Arabian Peninsula.
Al-Qāḍī related that some pronounced it ʿAmmān, with a fatḥah on the ʿayn and a doubled mīm, referring to ʿAmmān of al-Balqāʾ. This is incorrect.

١٠٥٥٦ — عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إنكم ستفتحون مصر، وهي أرض يسمى فيها القيراط، فإذا فتحتموها فأحسنوا إلى أهلها، فإن لهم ذمة ورحمًا - أو قال: ذمة وصهرًا - فإذا رأيت رجلين يختصمان فيها في موضع لبنة، فاخرج منها)).
فرأيت عبد الرحمن بن شرحبيل بن حسنة وأخاه ربيعة يختصمان في موضع لبنة، فخرجت منها.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٤٣/٢٢٧).
قوله: «ذمة ورحمًا»، يعني بالرحم أن أم إسماعيل، هاجر، كانت منهم.
وقوله: «ذمة وصهرًا»، يعني بالصهر أن أم إبراهيم بن محمد ﷺ، مارية القبطية، كانت منهم.

10556 — Abū Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“You will conquer Egypt, a land in which the qīrāṭ is commonly mentioned. When you conquer it, treat its people well, for they possess a covenant of protection and a bond of kinship—or he said: a covenant of protection and a bond through marriage. When you see two men disputing there over the space occupied by a brick, then leave it.”
Abū Dharr said:
I later saw ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah and his brother Rabīʿah disputing over the space occupied by a brick, so I left Egypt.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2543/227).
The words “a covenant of protection and a bond of kinship” refer to the fact that Hājar, the mother of Ismāʿīl, was from Egypt.
The words “a covenant of protection and a bond through marriage” refer to the fact that Māriyah the Copt, the mother of Ibrāhīm, the son of the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, was from Egypt.

10557 — Kaʿb ibn Mālik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When you conquer Egypt, instruct one another to treat the Copts well, for they possess a covenant of protection and a bond of kinship.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ Mushkil al-Āthār (2364) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (19/61), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (2/553).

١٠٥٥٩ — عن أبي هريرة أنه كان يحمل مع النبي ﷺ إداوة لوضوئه وحاجته، فبينما هو يتبعه بها، فقال: ((من هذا؟)). فقال: أنا أبو هريرة. فقال: ((ابغني أحجارًا أستنفض بها، ولا تأتني بعظم ولا بروثة)). فأتيته بأحجار أحملها في طرف ثوبي، حتى وضعتها إلى جنبه، ثم انصرفت. حتى إذا فرغ مشيت، فقلت: ما بال العظم والروثة؟ قال: ((هما من طعام الجن، وإنه أتاني وفد جن نصيبين، ونعم الجن، فسألوني الزاد، فدعوت اللّٰه لهم أن لا يمروا بعظم ولا بروثة إلا وجدوا عليها طعامًا)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٨٦٠).
وقوله: «نصيبين»: مدينة من مدن الجزيرة، تقع على الطريق بين الموصل والشام. وقيل: تقع على الحدود بين تركيا وسوريا، وهي داخل الحدود التركية.

english_source:
10559 — Abū Hurayrah used to carry a small vessel of water for the Prophet ﷺ to use for ablution and when relieving himself.
While Abū Hurayrah was following him with it, the Prophet ﷺ asked:
“Who is this?”
He replied:
“It is I, Abū Hurayrah.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Find some stones for me with which I may cleanse myself, but do not bring me a bone or animal dung.”
Abū Hurayrah said:
I brought him some stones, carrying them in the edge of my garment. I placed them beside him and then went away.
When he had finished, I walked with him and asked:
“What is the matter with bones and animal dung?”
He replied:
“They are among the food of the jinn. A delegation of the jinn of Naṣībīn came to me—and what excellent jinn they were—and asked me for provisions. I therefore supplicated to Allah for them that whenever they passed by a bone or animal dung, they would find food upon it.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3860).
Naṣībīn is a city in the region historically known as al-Jazīrah, situated on the route between Mosul and al-Shām. It is also said to lie near the modern border between Turkey and Syria, on the Turkish side.
